intent_lifecycle: A handled vertical key assigns stable selected identity and sets pending=true. More keys update that same selection and coalesce the repaint. The next process-table render consumes the flag, resolving identity against current rows. Snapshot-only or horizontal actions never set it. Reconciliation clears vanished identity before render, so consumption issues no list request. A later explicit vertical key legitimately selects a new process and creates new intent. A collapsed process panel does not call process_table, so intent waits for a subsequent visible render, just as the earlier list-owned request waited for list layout; this conclusion is source inspection, not a new collapse-interleaving test. No asynchronous boundary occurs between this resolver and synchronous list construction/prepaint.
